topic: Platform architecture, interoperability standards and cloud infrastructure for AICHEMIST's multi-domain digital twin SaaS (CEN extension): engine-agnostic sim kernel, live-twin vs simulation-twin modes, browser-first UX, cost-efficient multi-tenant GPU scheduling, LLM/agent control (status as of 2026-10-06)
executive_summary: Recommendation: build the platform layer in-house and adopt the engines. That means the control plane, scene/version service, twin connectors, web UX, MCP/agent layer, metering and multi-tenancy. Do NOT write a physics engine or renderer, because the open engines matured sharply in 2026. Make OpenUSD the canonical internal scene format. AOUSD Core Spec 1.0.1 was published 2025-12-12 under CC-BY-ND-4.0, and OpenUSD 26.08 shipped 2026-07-20 with UsdPhysics nested-rigid-body support, UsdValidation fixers, wasm builds and a Gaussian-splat UsdVolParticleField schema. Note that Core 1.0 standardizes only the data model, composition and value resolution, not UsdPhysics. Express physics as UsdPhysics plus backend-namespaced applied schemas (newton-usd-schemas Apache-2.0 v0.x, mjcPhysics, PhysxSchema). URDF, MJCF, SDFormat, glTF, FBX, PLY and SPZ are edge formats, handled by Apache-2.0 converters: newton-physics/urdf-usd-converter, mujoco-usd-converter and adobe/USD-Fileformat-plugins. The engine-agnostic seam already exists and should be copied, not invented. Isaac Lab 3.0.0-EA (2026-09-16, built for Isaac Sim 6.1, Newton 1.5.2, Warp 1.16) lets you pick physics=isaacsim_physx|ovphysx|newton_mjwarp and renderer=isaacsim_rtx|ovrtx|newton_renderer, and supports Kit-less execution with Warp/DLPack tensor paths. AICHEMIST's 'Sim Kernel API' should mirror that factory pattern. Suggested backend defaults: Newton 1.6.1 (Apache-2.0, Linux Foundation, 2026-10-05; MuJoCo-Warp/VBD/MPM/Kamino, deterministic paths since 1.4) for robot learning. ovphysx 0.6 (PhysX SDK 5.11, BSD-3, pip install) for USD-native industrial/vehicle rigid-body work. MuJoCo 3.15 CPU as the deterministic golden reference. ovrtx (pre-release, NVIDIA proprietary license) or Isaac Sim 6.1 for RTX camera/lidar/radar fidelity. NVIDIA itself is moving to modular headless libraries (ovrtx, ovphysx, ovstorage, announced GTC 2026, early access). Kit continues (Kit 110.3.0, 2026-08-28), but the Launcher (2025-10-01) and the old web-viewer-sample are deprecated. So confine Kit to where it is irreplaceable (Isaac Sim apps, Replicator SDG, ROS bridge, Kit App Streaming) and keep the physics path fully open-source to avoid lock-in. Live twins should flow OPC UA (open62541, MPL-2.0) / MQTT / ROS 2 (Lyrical Luth LTS, released 2026-05-22, EOL May 2031) into Kafka, then into a twin-state service (Eclipse Ditto-style with W3C WoT descriptions), then into a USD 'live session layer' plus a time-series DB (InfluxDB 3 or TimescaleDB). Simulation twins fork from a live snapshot for what-if, RL and synthetic-data runs. Standard formats per data class: MCAP (MIT; rosbag2 default) for raw logs, LeRobotDataset v3 (many episodes per Parquet/MP4, Hub streaming) for training exports, FMI 3.0.2 FMUs plus SSP for vehicle and factory system models. UX should be browser-first and hybrid. The default is client-side WebGPU/WebGL with zero server GPU cost (three.js r186, Babylon.js 9.29 with an OpenUSD WASM loader, PlayCanvas 2.23 splat LOD streaming, Spark for 3DGS). Server-side WebRTC pixel streaming (Kit livestream, own NVENC pipeline, UE Pixel Streaming 2 for UE5.7/5.8) is used only for RTX-fidelity sessions and scales to zero when idle. Compute runs on Kubernetes + GPU Operator v26.7 + KAI Scheduler (Apache-2.0, the open-sourced Run:ai scheduler core: gang scheduling, fractional GPU, hierarchical DRF queues). Add Ray 2.59 for RL and data pipelines, SkyPilot for multi-cloud spot burst, and optionally Slinky (Slurm-on-K8s) and NVIDIA OSMO (Apache-2.0) for physical-AI workflow DAGs. Split GPU pools by capability. RT-core GPUs (L40S at $1.861/h, RTX PRO 6000 at $3.363/h on AWS us-east-1 on-demand; Seoul about 23% higher) handle rendering, streaming and SDG. H100/B200 ($6.88/GPU-h for H100) handle training and render-free physics only. Never time-slice GPUs across tenants. Version scenes as content-hashed USD layer stacks, and make replay reproducible by pinning container digest, driver, GPU SKU, seeds and an MCAP input log. lakeFS moved to BSL 1.1 in v1.87.0 (Sept 2026), so treat it as license-sensitive. Expose everything through a first-party MCP server plus a sandboxed USD code-generating agent with validation gates. Community MCPs (isaac-sim-mcp, blender-mcp, unreal-mcp) execute arbitrary code and are prototypes only. The biggest commercial risk is licensing: Kit, ovrtx and the Omniverse blueprints are under NVIDIA proprietary terms, so hosted-SaaS rights must be negotiated with NVIDIA before GA.

options.name: OpenUSD + AOUSD Core Specification
options.category: Canonical scene description / interchange standard
options.status_as_of_2026: AOUSD Core Spec v1.0.1 published 2025-12-12. It is the only normative AOUSD spec so far and covers the data model, composition and value resolution. UsdPhysics and other domain schemas are not yet normative. AOUSD reported member/industrial momentum in March 2026. Pixar OpenUSD 26.08 (2026-07-20): composition load up to 80% faster on heavy rigs, LOD schemas, UsdProfiles. 26.05 (2026-04-24): Hydra 2 scene-index path is the default. 26.03 (2026-02-24): wasm32/wasm64 builds, UsdVolParticleField (3D Gaussian splats), UsdPhysics nested rigid bodies and kinematic articulation. 25.11: OpenExec moved into core.
options.license_and_cost: OpenUSD code is under the Tomorrow Open Source Technology License (Apache-2.0-derived), free. AOUSD spec text is CC-BY-ND-4.0. AOUSD membership is optional and paid.
strengths: De-facto industry standard: NVIDIA, Apple, Autodesk, Adobe, Siemens and Trimble ecosystems
Non-destructive layer composition maps naturally to multi-user edits, live-state overlays and scene versioning
UsdPhysics is the common physics vocabulary read by PhysX/ovphysx, Newton and MuJoCo converters
WASM builds and a Babylon.js OpenUSD loader enable a browser path
UsdValidation framework with fixers can serve as a CI gate for agent-authored scenes
weaknesses: Steep learning curve, and composition semantics are hard for app developers
Physics, sensor and actuator semantics are still vendor-namespaced (physx*, newton*, mjc*), with no normative physics spec yet
Large-stage streaming to browsers still needs conversion or LOD (glTF or splats)
options.best_fit: Canonical internal representation for all scenes, robots, vehicles, factories, materials and semantic labels.

options.name: Newton physics engine + newton-usd-schemas + URDF/MJCF->USD converters
options.category: Physics backend (GPU, open source) + USD physics schema extension
options.status_as_of_2026: Newton 1.0 GA at GTC in March 2026, after a beta first shown in Sept 2025. Latest is v1.6.1 (2026-10-05). Earlier steps: v1.6.0 (2026-09-10) made hydroelastic contacts 33-37% faster and added OpenUSD particles. v1.4.0 (2026-07-16) added coupled solvers (MuJoCo, Kamino, VBD) and deterministic paths for bit-exact repeated rollouts. v1.2.0 added a composable actuator subsystem with USD schema support. The project is hosted by the Linux Foundation, co-developed by Disney Research, Google DeepMind and NVIDIA. newton-usd-schemas is v0.x and marked experimental (codeless schemas extending UsdPhysics). The org also ships urdf-usd-converter and mujoco-usd-converter.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0 for code, CC-BY-4.0 for docs. Free.
strengths: Multi-solver (MuJoCo-Warp, VBD cloth/cables, implicit MPM, Kamino) behind one model API
Built on Warp, so it runs batched on GPU and integrates differentiably with PyTorch/JAX via Warp
Vendor-neutral governance under the Linux Foundation
Native backend in Isaac Lab 3.0 (newton_mjwarp), with a Kit-less path
weaknesses: Fast release cadence (monthly minors) and schema v0.x means API churn
Requires NVIDIA CUDA GPUs; no AMD or Apple path
Vehicle, tire and powertrain models are thinner than PhysX vehicle or dedicated AV simulators
options.best_fit: Default physics backend for robot learning (locomotion, manipulation, deformables) and batched simulation twins.

options.name: NVIDIA Omniverse libraries: ovphysx / ovrtx / ovstorage
options.category: Headless modular physics / RTX sensor rendering / storage libraries
options.status_as_of_2026: Announced at GTC 2026 as headless-first C APIs with C++ and Python bindings, early access on GitHub and NGC, with production API stability promised 'later this year'. The SIGGRAPH 2026 coverage was not fetchable here. ovphysx 0.6 maps to PhysX SDK 5.11.0 (0.5 to 5.10) and is installed with pip install ovphysx; it offers USD physics with DLPack tensor interop. ovrtx is pre-release: a C11 + Python 3.10-3.13 SDK for camera, lidar and radar on Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64/aarch64, shipped as PyPI wheels. ovstorage is pre-release and not enterprise-supported: a plugin storage client for file, HTTP, S3, GCS, Azure, OpenDAL, Nucleus and Omniverse Storage Service, with an MCP server and agent skills.
options.license_and_cost: ovphysx/PhysX: BSD-3-Clause. ovstorage: Apache-2.0 (agent skills CC-BY-4.0; vendored service material proprietary). ovrtx: NVIDIA Software License Agreement + Product-Specific Terms for NVIDIA AI Products, which is proprietary, so hosted-SaaS terms must be confirmed.
strengths: Lets you embed NVIDIA physics and RTX sensors into your own services without the Kit app framework, which suits CI/CD and K8s
Same backends Isaac Lab 3.0 selects (physics=ovphysx, renderer=ovrtx)
ovstorage treats Nucleus as just one backend, which aligns with an object-storage-first design
weaknesses: Pre-1.0, and NVIDIA states APIs may change between releases
ovrtx is closed-license and needs RTX (RT-core) GPUs
ovstorage is not accepting external contributions and is not enterprise-supported
options.best_fit: ovphysx: USD-native industrial and vehicle rigid/articulated physics. ovrtx: high-fidelity sensor simulation and SDG workers. ovstorage: optional client abstraction.

options.name: NVIDIA Omniverse Kit SDK / Kit App Template / Kit App Streaming / NVCF / Nucleus
options.category: Full application framework + streaming + collaboration server
options.status_as_of_2026: Kit App Template changelog shows 110.3.0 (2026-08-28, with a kit-upgrade agent skill for 106-110 migrations), 110.1.0 (2026-04-06, versioned packages), 109.0.1 (2025-12-04, ARM64, raised driver floor) and 108.0.0 (2025-08-12, 'Omniverse Cloud Streaming' renamed 'NVCF Streaming', omni.kit.livestream.app). Templates: Kit Service, Base Editor, USD Composer, USD Explorer, USD Viewer (built for streaming). Kit App Streaming (OKAS) is a self-managed K8s/Helm reference; NVCF is the managed option. Launcher deprecated 2025-10-01. web-viewer-sample deprecated in favour of the OV Web SDK WebRTC sample. Nucleus continues, but the 26H1 storage stack and ovstorage reposition it as one backend.
options.license_and_cost: NVIDIA Software License + Omniverse Product-Specific Terms (proprietary). Enterprise production deployment historically needed Omniverse Enterprise per-GPU licensing. Current price not verified (low confidence).
strengths: Fastest route to a polished RTX editor, viewer and streamed app
Reference blueprints exist: the DSX AI-factory twin (React portal + Kit WebRTC livestream + OKAS/NVCF, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) and the CAE fluid twin (React + WebRTC + NIM/Triton surrogate)
Mature extension ecosystem (400+ extensions)
weaknesses: Heavy runtime and a GPU per session, which makes streaming costly
Proprietary, with frequent major versions (108 to 110 in about 12 months)
Lock-in to NVIDIA hardware and licensing; template is based on a Kit 'feature branch'
options.best_fit: Premium high-fidelity editing and viewing sessions and Isaac Sim-based workflows. Not suited to the always-on default UX or batch workers.

options.name: Isaac Sim 6.1 / Isaac Lab 3.0
options.category: Robotics simulator app + robot-learning framework (reference for backend abstraction)
options.status_as_of_2026: Isaac Sim v6.0.0 GA (June 2026), v6.0.1 (June 22), v6.1.0 GA (Sept 10, 2026), v7.0.0a1 (Sept 18, 2026). Python 3.12, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 or Windows 11. Minimum RTX 4080 or A40; L40S recommended. Isaac Lab 3.0.0-EA (Sept 16, 2026) has multi-backend physics (isaacsim_physx, ovphysx, newton_mjwarp), renderers (isaacsim_rtx, ovrtx, newton_renderer), five visualizers (Newton GL, Newton RTX, Kit, Viser, Rerun) and a unified 'isaaclab train'. Breaking change: quaternions go from (w,x,y,z) to (x,y,z,w). The IsaacSim-ros_workspaces README lists only Humble and Jazzy.
options.license_and_cost: Isaac Sim source is Apache-2.0, but it depends on the Kit SDK (NVIDIA proprietary). Isaac Lab is BSD-3; isaaclab_mimic is Apache-2.0. Free.
strengths: Most complete open robotics sim stack: RTX sensors, ROS bridge, Replicator SDG, importers, RL/IL (Mimic)
Isaac Lab 3.0's factory pattern is a ready blueprint for an engine-agnostic sim kernel
Kit-less Newton mode allows light containers
weaknesses: Major-version churn (5.x, then 6.x, then 7.0 alpha within about 15 months) and breaking API changes
No official ROS 2 Lyrical workspace yet, per the repo README
Full app needs RT-core GPUs, so it cannot render on H100/B200
options.best_fit: High-fidelity robot sensor simulation, SDG and RL/IL training environments. Wrap it as one backend of AICHEMIST's Sim Kernel, not as the platform itself.

options.name: MuJoCo 3.x / MuJoCo Warp / MJCF
options.category: Physics backend + robot description format
options.status_as_of_2026: MuJoCo 3.15.0 (2026-10-05). 3.14.0 added archive resource providers. 3.13.0 added Python 3.15 and a 'discrete' integrator. 3.12.0 added a PID actuator. MuJoCo Warp is version-locked (3.15.0). The repo has src/experimental/usd with an mjcPhysics schema, an MJCF plugin and a USD writer.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0, free.
strengths: Deterministic CPU simulation is the golden reference for replay and regression
Huge model zoo (Menagerie) and MJCF is the lingua franca of RL research
MuJoCo Warp powers Newton's main solver
weaknesses: USD support is experimental
Limited rendering and sensor realism
options.best_fit: Golden-reference and validation backend, plus MJCF import/export for customer compatibility.

options.name: URDF / SDFormat / glTF 2.0 + converter plugins
options.category: Edge interchange formats
options.status_as_of_2026: SDFormat 16 ships with Gazebo Jetty. glTF 2.0: KHR_physics_rigid_bodies is still 'Review Draft'; the extensions index lists KHR_interactivity and KHR_gaussian_splatting among ratified extensions (medium confidence). adobe/USD-Fileformat-plugins (Apache-2.0) covers glTF/GLB, FBX, OBJ, PLY, SBSAR, SPZ and STL. NVIDIA usd-exchange SDK (Apache-2.0) is for writing USD connectors.
options.license_and_cost: Open specs. Converter plugins are Apache-2.0.
strengths: glTF/GLB is the best format for web delivery
URDF is universal in ROS
SPZ/PLY carry Gaussian splats from NeRF/3DGS capture, matching CEN's photo-to-3D pipeline
weaknesses: URDF has no closed loops and weak sensor/material semantics
glTF physics is not ratified
Round-trips lose information
options.best_fit: Import/export edges only. Compile USD to glTF/splat LOD bundles for browser viewing.

options.name: ROS 2 (Humble / Jazzy / Kilted / Lyrical) + rmw_zenoh + rosbag2/MCAP
options.category: Robot middleware / live-twin connectivity / logging
options.status_as_of_2026: Lyrical Luth released 2026-05-22, LTS to May 2031, the 12th release. It adds native buffers in the Fast DDS RMW for GPU/accelerated memory transport. Jazzy EOL May 2029, Humble EOL May 2027, Kilted EOL Dec 2026. The next release, 'Makoa Mata-mata', is due May 2027. rmw_zenoh needs a Zenoh router (multicast discovery off by default) and is not interoperable with zenoh-plugin-ros2dds. rosbag2's default storage is MCAP.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0, free.
strengths: Universal robot integration; sim and real share the same interfaces (use_sim_time /clock)
Zenoh suits WAN and cloud links from customer sites to the twin cloud better than DDS multicast
MCAP is indexable, compressible and multi-language
weaknesses: Version fragmentation across customers (Humble, Jazzy and Lyrical all coexist)
DDS discovery is hostile to NAT/cloud, so a bridge or Zenoh is needed
options.best_fit: Robot live-twin ingest, HIL/SIL, and canonical robot log format (MCAP).

options.name: Gazebo Jetty (gz-sim 10) + ros_gz
options.category: Open-source ROS-native simulator (alternative backend)
options.status_as_of_2026: Jetty (gz-sim 10, SDFormat 16) is the current LTS, released around late 2025 (exact date unverified). ros_gz pairings: Humble-Fortress, Jazzy-Harmonic, Kilted-Ionic, Lyrical-Jetty, Rolling-Jetty.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0, free.
strengths: ROS-native, and many customers already have SDF worlds
Runs CPU-only, which is cheap for CI and logic tests
weaknesses: Lower visual and sensor fidelity
Not GPU-batched for RL at scale
options.best_fit: Optional plug-in backend for ROS customers and CI smoke tests. Not a flagship backend.

options.name: FMI 3.0 / SSP / Modelica (OpenModelica)
options.category: System-level co-simulation standards (vehicles, powertrain, HVAC, PLC/process models)
options.status_as_of_2026: FMI 3.0.2 (2024-11-27) is the latest maintenance release, adding clocks, arrays, terminals and icons, and layered standards. No FMI 3.1 was found. SSP 1.0 and 2.0 maintenance branches exist (2.0 release date not verified). OpenModelica 1.27.x (2026) is still FMI 2-focused; FMI 3 support is promised for 1.28.0 (planned end of 2026).
options.license_and_cost: FMI/SSP standards are free (SSP schemas BSD-2, docs CC-BY-SA). OpenModelica is OSMC-PL/GPL. Commercial tools (Dymola, Simulink) export FMUs.
strengths: Lets customers bring their existing validated vehicle and plant models as black-box FMUs
SSP describes system wiring and parameters tool-independently
weaknesses: Fixed-step co-simulation with rigid-body physics needs a careful master algorithm
OpenModelica lags on FMI 3
options.best_fit: Vehicle dynamics/powertrain, factory process and energy models plugged into the co-simulation orchestrator alongside the physics backend.

options.name: OPC UA (open62541) / MQTT / Kafka / Eclipse Ditto
options.category: Industrial live-twin ingestion and twin-state management
options.status_as_of_2026: open62541 v1.5.9, v1.4.21 and v1.3.22 released together in October 2026. It supports PubSub with encryption and TLS MQTT PubSub. Eclipse Ditto 3.9.7 (2026, fixing CVE-2026-84175 and CVE-2026-82958); 3.9.0 added WoT Thing Description support plus MQTT/Kafka connectivity. Kafka 4.x is KRaft-only (not verified this session).
options.license_and_cost: open62541 MPL-2.0. Ditto EPL-2.0. Kafka Apache-2.0. MQTT brokers (Mosquitto EPL/EDL, EMQX) are open source; managed options are paid.
strengths: Standard factory connectivity (OPC UA) plus lightweight IoT (MQTT)
Ditto provides twin shadow state, a policy/ACL model and search out of the box
weaknesses: Ditto is JVM/MongoDB-heavy
Mapping the OPC UA information model to USD prims needs a custom mapping layer
options.best_fit: Live-twin state sync for factories, warehouses, ships and fleets.

options.name: Time-series DBs: InfluxDB 3 / TimescaleDB
options.category: Live-twin history and telemetry store
options.status_as_of_2026: InfluxDB 3 v3.11.4 (2026-09-04) uses an object-storage and Parquet architecture. TimescaleDB 2.x offers hypertables, a columnstore with 90%+ compression, and continuous aggregates.
options.license_and_cost: InfluxDB 3 Core is open source (MIT/Apache, not re-verified); Enterprise is paid. TimescaleDB is Apache-2.0 core plus the Timescale License (TSL) for advanced features, so check SaaS-hosting restrictions.
strengths: Parquet/object storage (Influx 3) fits a data lake
Timescale is plain Postgres, so it can share the platform's metadata DB skills
weaknesses: The TSL restricts offering Timescale as a DBaaS
InfluxDB 3 Core is young
options.best_fit: TimescaleDB for an MVP (Postgres ops reuse); evaluate InfluxDB 3 or Iceberg for large fleets.

options.name: Dataset/log formats: MCAP, rosbag2, LeRobotDataset v3, Rerun
options.category: Episode logging, training-data export, debugging visualization
options.status_as_of_2026: MCAP (MIT; libraries in C++, Go, Python, TS, Swift, Rust) is the rosbag2 default. LeRobotDataset v3.0 stores many episodes per Parquet/MP4 file, with meta/info.json, stats.json, chunked episode metadata, StreamingLeRobotDataset and a v2.1 converter; dataset.finalize() is required. LeRobot v0.6.1 (Aug 2026). Rerun 0.38.1 (2026-09-17) has a ROS 2 MCAP timeline, experimental Gaussian splats and a catalog for larger-than-RAM files. Lichtblick (MPL-2.0, open-core) is a fork of Foxglove Studio.
options.license_and_cost: MCAP MIT. LeRobot Apache-2.0. Rerun MIT/Apache (not explicitly verified). Lichtblick MPL-2.0.
strengths: MCAP to LeRobot v3 conversion links real and sim logs to VLA/IL training
LeRobot v3 streaming from the Hub matches the marketplace distribution model
weaknesses: LeRobot API churn (breaking module renames in 0.6.x)
Video codec settings affect training fidelity
options.best_fit: MCAP is canonical for raw multi-sensor logs (sim and real). LeRobot v3 is the canonical export for robot-learning datasets. Rerun or Lichtblick serve as embedded debug viewers.

options.name: Kubernetes + NVIDIA GPU Operator + KAI Scheduler (Run:ai OSS core) + DRA
options.category: GPU cluster orchestration and multi-tenant scheduling
options.status_as_of_2026: GPU Operator v26.7.1 (Sept 2026), released on a 26.3/26.7 cadence. KAI Scheduler v0.18.2 (Oct 2026): gang scheduling, NvFractions GPU-memory fractional sharing, hierarchical queues with DRF and reclaim, topology-aware placement, DRA accounting. NVIDIA DRA driver (Apache-2.0): ComputeDomains (MNNVL/IMEX) are supported; DRA-based GPU allocation is still 'not yet officially supported'.
options.license_and_cost: All Apache-2.0 and free. Run:ai commercial control plane is paid (price not verified).
strengths: Fractional GPUs and per-tenant queues are exactly what interactive sim sessions plus batch jobs need
Scheduling for RL and distributed training is gang-safe
weaknesses: Fractional and time-sliced GPUs do not isolate memory or faults, so they are unsafe across tenants
DRA GPU path not yet GA in NVIDIA's driver
options.best_fit: Core scheduler for the AICHEMIST cluster: queues per tenant and tier, fractions only within a tenant.

options.name: NVIDIA OSMO
options.category: Physical-AI workflow orchestrator (SDG, sim, train, HIL DAGs)
options.status_as_of_2026: Open source on GitHub. Release 6.3.1 (June 2026) brought ConfigMap configuration, gateway TLS and deploy scripts for AKS, EKS and microk8s. 6.2.8 added OAuth2 RBAC and NVLink topology-aware scheduling. Runs locally on KIND or on cloud K8s.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0, free.
strengths: Purpose-built for Isaac SDG, training, RL and HIL pipelines in YAML
Supports heterogeneous compute, including edge devices
weaknesses: Overlaps with Argo, Flyte and Ray
NVIDIA-centric roadmap
options.best_fit: Optional internal pipeline engine for SDG to train to evaluate. Alternatively use Argo Workflows plus Ray if you want vendor neutrality.

options.name: Ray (KubeRay) / SkyPilot / Slurm via Slinky
options.category: Distributed compute, multi-cloud burst, HPC-style training
options.status_as_of_2026: Ray 2.59.0 (Oct 2026): Ray Data LLM and Serve LLM are GA; 2.58 added an experimental gVisor-based Ray Sandbox and TPU support in Ray Train. SkyPilot (Apache-2.0) covers K8s, Slurm and 20+ clouds with spot failover, autostop and binpacking. Slinky slurm-operator 1.3.x (Apache-2.0, SchedMD) supports K8s 1.35-1.37 and Slurm 25.11 or newer.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0, free. Anyscale is paid.
strengths: Ray suits RL rollouts plus SDG data pipelines
SkyPilot cuts cost by chasing spot capacity across clouds, including Korean data residency choices
Slinky gives ML researchers familiar sbatch on the same K8s cluster
weaknesses: Three schedulers add operational complexity, so pick one primary (KAI) and treat the others as job frontends
options.best_fit: Ray for RL and data, SkyPilot for burst, Slinky only if the research team demands Slurm.

options.name: Server-side pixel streaming: Omniverse Kit livestream (WebRTC) / UE Pixel Streaming 2 / Selkies
options.category: Remote rendering to the browser
options.status_as_of_2026: Kit uses omni.kit.livestream.app (WebRTC) with OKAS on K8s or NVCF; the old web-viewer-sample is deprecated in favour of the OV Web SDK. UE Pixel Streaming 2 (introduced UE 5.5): the infrastructure repo supports UE5.8 (current) and UE5.7, UE5.6 is end-of-life; it includes the Cirrus signalling server and an SFU, MIT licensed. Selkies (MPL-2.0): WebSocket by default with WebRTC opt-in, Ubuntu 26.04 desktop containers; the project is asking for maintainers.
options.license_and_cost: Software is free (Kit is proprietary). Cost is GPU-hours: roughly 1 L40S-class GPU per heavy RTX session, about $1.86-2.29/h on-demand on AWS.
strengths: Full RTX fidelity on any thin client
Selkies can stream CEN's existing browser virtual OS/desktop workspace
weaknesses: Highest per-user cost
Latency from Korea to US regions
Needs TURN/SFU infrastructure
options.best_fit: Premium, on-demand high-fidelity sessions and full desktop workspaces, with auto-suspend.

options.name: Client-side web 3D: three.js / Babylon.js / PlayCanvas / Spark / Viser
options.category: Browser rendering (WebGPU/WebGL) for the default UX
options.status_as_of_2026: three.js r186 (Sept 2026): WebGPU compute (compileComputeAsync) and TSL improvements. Babylon.js 9.29.0 (Oct 1, 2026); 9.26 (Sept 2026) added an OpenUSD WebAssembly loader, with Gaussian-splat streaming/LOD and KHR_interactivity. PlayCanvas 2.23.0 (Oct 2026): distance-based splat LOD and streamed loading. Spark 2.x (MIT, World Labs): a three.js 3DGS renderer supporting PLY, SPZ, SPLAT, KSPLAT and SOG. Viser (Apache-2.0): Python-driven web 3D, one of Isaac Lab 3.0's visualizers.
options.license_and_cost: MIT (three.js, PlayCanvas engine, Spark) and Apache-2.0 (Babylon.js, Viser). No server GPU cost.
strengths: Zero marginal GPU cost and instant load, the right default for dashboards, live-twin monitoring, annotation and marketplace previews
3DGS lets photoreal captured environments run on laptops and phones
weaknesses: No RTX path tracing or physically accurate sensor simulation
Large USD stages need server-side baking to glTF and splat LODs
options.best_fit: Default UI. Babylon.js if the browser reads USD directly; three.js + Spark if you want the largest ecosystem and splats.

recommendations_for_aichemist: BUILD vs ADOPT. Build in-house: the control plane (tenancy, auth, metering into CEN tokens), scene/version service, twin-connector service, Sim Kernel API, web UX, first-party MCP server and agent, and dataset/marketplace integration. Adopt as pluggable backends: Newton, ovphysx/PhysX, MuJoCo, ovrtx/Isaac Sim RTX, Gazebo, CARLA and FMUs. Never fork or write a physics engine; contribute upstream to Newton (Linux Foundation, Apache-2.0) instead.

REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE, 8 layers. L0 Infra: K8s + GPU Operator + KAI Scheduler, with node pools RT-render (L40S / RTX PRO 6000), Compute-train (H100/H200/B200) and Light (L4/CPU). L1 Data: S3-compatible object store (canonical blobs), Postgres (metadata, scene commits), Kafka (event backbone), TSDB (telemetry), Iceberg/DVC (datasets), model registry. L2 Scene model: OpenUSD stage service with validation. L3 Sim Kernel: engine-agnostic physics, sensor and co-sim orchestrator. L4 Twin runtime: Live mode, Simulation mode and Shadow/HIL mode. L5 Learning: Isaac Lab 3 / Newton envs, LeRobot, Ray RLlib, SDG pipelines, evaluation harness. L6 Platform APIs: REST/gRPC + Python SDK + MCP. L7 UX: browser-first WebGPU client, on-demand WebRTC streaming, Jupyter/VS Code in the CEN workspace. L8 Agents: LLM planner + sandboxed USD code generation + validation gates.

CANONICAL INTERNAL STANDARDS. Scene, assets, robots and vehicles: OpenUSD (pin a version per platform release, e.g. 26.08), with UsdPhysics as the portable core plus namespaced applied schemas (newton:*, mjc:*, physx*) for backend extras, and UsdSemantics labels for SDG. Raw logs: MCAP. Robot-learning datasets: LeRobotDataset v3 (export COCO/KITTI/nuScenes-style for perception). System models: FMI 3.0 FMUs + SSP. Twin metadata: W3C WoT Thing Description (as in Ditto) mapped 1:1 to USD prim paths. Web delivery: glTF/GLB + SPZ/SOG splats compiled from USD. Edge-only formats: URDF, MJCF, SDF, FBX, OBJ, STL, OpenDRIVE, OpenSCENARIO, OSI.

ENGINE-AGNOSTIC SIM KERNEL API. Copy Isaac Lab 3.0's factory pattern: backend = {physics: newton_mjwarp | ovphysx | mujoco_cpu | gazebo | fmu}, renderer = {ovrtx | isaacsim_rtx | newton_gl | none}. The minimal ABI: load(usd_stage_ref, backend_cfg); step(dt, substeps, n_envs); get_state/set_state as Warp/DLPack tensors; apply_actions; render(sensor_ids) to tensors; contacts(); snapshot() / restore(blob); set_seed(); capabilities(). Ship a conformance suite (falling box, pendulum, Franka pick, wheeled vehicle, cloth) that compares backends within tolerances and runs in CI on every backend upgrade.

LIVE-TWIN vs SIMULATION-TWIN. Live mode: edge gateway (OPC UA via open62541, MQTT, ROS 2 over Zenoh or a DDS bridge) feeds Kafka, then the twin-state service (latest state + WoT model), then a per-twin USD session layer that overrides only transforms, joint states and signals at 10-60 Hz and is pushed to browsers over WebSocket. History goes to the TSDB. Simulation mode: headless batched runs faster than real time, on spot. Fork-from-live: snapshot the live state, then calibrate (system ID / parameter estimation), then run what-if or RL in Simulation mode on a scene branch, then compare predictions against later live data to score twin fidelity. Shadow/HIL mode: run real controllers against the sim with use_sim_time and a lockstep clock.

BROWSER-FIRST UX. Make the WebGPU/WebGL client the default: Babylon.js 9.x if reading USD client-side, or three.js r186 + Spark for splats and glTF. Bake USD into glTF/splat LOD tiles server-side on asset commit. Offer a 'High-fidelity view' button that launches a WebRTC pixel-stream session: Kit USD Viewer template with livestream, or your own ovrtx + NVENC + WebRTC service. Put sessions behind a session manager with 5-10 minute idle auto-suspend and warm pools. Reuse CEN's browser virtual OS/JupyterLab (Selkies-style) for code-first users. Host streaming GPUs in Seoul for Korean customers, since latency matters more than the roughly 23% price premium.

COST-EFFICIENT GPU SCHEDULING. Use KAI hierarchical queues: tenant, then tier (interactive / batch / training), with guaranteed quotas for paid tiers and preemptible over-quota. Run batch SDG, RL and evaluation on spot with frequent checkpointing (Newton/Isaac Lab state snapshots + MCAP), and burst through SkyPilot across AWS, GCP and Korean CSPs. Route render-free physics RL (Newton/MuJoCo Warp) to the cheapest adequate GPU: often an L40S or RTX PRO 6000 beats an H100 on price per env-step for simulation. Benchmark steps/s/$ per backend and GPU monthly. Reserve H100/B200 for VLA/foundation-model training. Use a reserved or on-prem RTX PRO 6000 baseline for steady interactive load. Meter GPU-seconds per tenant from DCGM and KAI into CEN tokens.

MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION. Give each paying tenant whole GPUs or MIG slices (RTX PRO 6000 / H100). Allow time-slicing and KAI fractional sharing only within one tenant's own jobs, or for free-tier previews on dedicated 'untrusted' node pools. Run user code and agent-generated code in Kata Containers or gVisor (Ray Sandbox is experimental). Isolate networks per tenant namespace. Encrypt buckets per tenant. Add data-residency tags (KR / US / EU) enforced by the scheduler.

DETERMINISM AND REPLAY. Define a 'Run Manifest': scene commit hash (USD layer-stack content hashes), asset blob hashes, container image digest, backend + version, GPU SKU + driver, seeds, dt and substeps, plus the MCAP input log (actions and external live data). Use Newton's deterministic mode (v1.4+) or MuJoCo CPU for bit-exact regression. Use tolerance-based comparison for GPU PhysX and RTX. Store manifests with every dataset and model for lineage, which also supports enterprise audits and the CEN marketplace provenance story.

SCENE VERSIONING. Implement a thin 'scene commit' service rather than adopting lakeFS (now BSL 1.1). Each edit or session writes its own USD layer; commits are immutable manifests; branches are pointers; merges work at layer granularity with conflict detection on prim paths. Offer Git/Git-LFS and Perforce sync connectors for enterprise customers, and Iceberg or DVC snapshots for datasets.

OBSERVABILITY. Use OpenTelemetry traces from job submit through scheduler, sim step, render and encode. Use Prometheus + DCGM exporter for GPU utilisation, memory, NVENC and power. Track sim-specific SLOs: real-time factor, steps/s/GPU, solver NaN/explosion detectors, contact counts, streaming RTT and frame drops. Use Rerun or Lichtblick embedded for episode debugging. Track cost per job and per tenant on dashboards.

AGENT / MCP LAYER. Expose a first-party MCP server (spec rev 2026-07-28) with typed, permissioned tools: scene.search/query/diff, scene.apply_ops (high-level USD ops, not raw exec), asset.search (marketplace), sim.run/sweep, job.submit/status, twin.query/forecast, dataset.export, policy.evaluate. Add a code-generating authoring agent that writes USD Python in a sandbox. Gate its output with UsdValidation, physics sanity checks (mass/inertia, interpenetration, joint limits) and a backend smoke test before the commit lands on a branch; a human approves merges. Use NVIDIA kit-usd-agents MCPs for API grounding. Wrap ros-mcp-server behind tenant ACLs for robot connections. Do not expose community MCPs with arbitrary exec to tenants.

NVIDIA LICENSING AND LOCK-IN. Before GA, obtain written NVIDIA terms for hosting Kit apps, ovrtx and Isaac Sim (Kit runtime) as multi-tenant SaaS (Omniverse Enterprise / OEM / partner program). Keep a fully open fallback path: Newton/MuJoCo/ovphysx (BSD) physics + newton_gl / web renderers + Gazebo. That way the core product survives a licensing change, with RTX fidelity sold as a premium tier.

ROADMAP. M0-3 (MVP): USD scene service + importers (URDF/MJCF/glTF via converters), Sim Kernel with Newton + ovphysx + MuJoCo, batch jobs on K8s/KAI, three.js/Babylon viewer, MCAP logging, LeRobot v3 export, first-party MCP (read and run tools). M3-9: ovrtx/Isaac Sim RTX sensors and SDG, WebRTC premium sessions, Isaac Lab 3 training templates (RL + IL/VLA fine-tuning), live-twin connectors (ROS 2/Zenoh, MQTT, OPC UA) + TSDB, scene commits and branches, authoring agent with validation gates. M9-18: FMI/SSP co-simulation, vehicle module (OpenDRIVE/OpenSCENARIO/OSI), fork-from-live calibration, enterprise on-prem/VPC deployment (Helm), MIG-based tenancy, marketplace integration of SimReady assets and datasets, SOC2/ISMS-P.

TEAM, about 22-26 FTE by month 12 (estimate). Platform/infra/SRE 4 (K8s, KAI, networking, security). Sim kernel and physics integration 4 (Newton/PhysX/MuJoCo, conformance, determinism). Rendering/sensors/streaming 3 (ovrtx, WebRTC, NVENC). Web 3D and frontend 3. Data/ML (SDG, RL/IL/VLA, LeRobot) 4. IIoT/live-twin integration 2. LLM/agent/MCP 2. PM, solutions and DevRel 2. Hire at least one USD expert and one OPC UA/industrial engineer early.

INFRA BUDGET (rough, derived from AWS list prices). Dev/staging: 1x 8-GPU RTX PRO 6000 node, about $24k/month on-demand or much less spot/reserved, or buy on-prem. Early production (approx. 20 concurrent premium sessions + batch): about $40-80k/month blended with 40-60% on spot. Training bursts: 8x H100 at about $40k/month if always on, so schedule bursts instead. Default to client-side rendering to keep the GPU bill proportional to premium usage.
risks: NVIDIA proprietary licensing: Kit SDK, ovrtx and the Omniverse blueprints are under NVIDIA SLA / Product-Specific Terms. Rights to host them as multi-tenant SaaS and to charge tokens for their use are unverified and could block or tax the premium fidelity tier.

API churn in early-access and fast-moving components: ovrtx, ovphysx and ovstorage are pre-1.0; newton-usd-schemas is v0.x experimental; Isaac Lab 3.0 changed quaternion order and data types; Kit went through about 3 majors in 12 months. Integration maintenance could consume a large share of engineering time without a strict adapter layer and conformance suite.

No normative physics standard: AOUSD Core 1.0 excludes UsdPhysics, and glTF physics is still a review draft. Cross-engine physics portability depends on vendor schemas, so the same USD asset can behave differently on Newton vs PhysX vs MuJoCo.

GPU determinism limits: bit-exact replay is only realistic on CPU MuJoCo or Newton's deterministic paths on identical hardware and drivers. RTX rendering and GPU PhysX need tolerance-based validation, which complicates audit and replay claims.

Multi-tenant GPU security: time-slicing and fractional sharing give no memory or fault isolation, and MIG availability on RT-core GPUs in Korean clouds is unverified. Agent-generated and user code is an RCE surface (community MCPs explicitly execute arbitrary Python).

Cost blow-up from pixel streaming: a dedicated L40S per session is about $1.9-2.3/h. Without client-side default rendering, auto-suspend and warm pools, gross margins on subscriptions can go negative.

License drift in the open-source stack: lakeFS moved to BSL 1.1 (v1.87.0), Foxglove Studio went closed (hence the Lichtblick fork), and TimescaleDB TSL restricts DBaaS. Every embedded dependency needs SPDX tracking and license review.
ROS 2 fragmentation: customers on Humble, Jazzy and Lyrical at once, and Isaac Sim's ROS workspace lists only Humble and Jazzy. Bridges must be multi-distro and Zenoh/DDS-aware.
NVIDIA hardware lock-in: Newton, Warp, ovrtx and Isaac all need CUDA/RTX, so there is no AMD/Intel fallback for GPU physics or rendering. Supply and price shocks pass straight through.

Data residency and latency: Korean public-sector and manufacturing customers may require domestic hosting. Seoul GPU prices are about 23-38% higher and capacity for new SKUs (RTX PRO 6000, B200) may be limited.

Research verification gap: the web-search budget ran out after a few queries, and many primary vendor domains (developer.nvidia.com, docs.omniverse.nvidia.com, docs.ros.org, aousd.org, gazebosim.org, AWS docs) were egress-blocked. Several 2026 facts were verified only through GitHub pages; GitHub release dates without a year were inferred as 2026 from version context.
